speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've experienced a rear-end collision resulting in right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning; tell me, can you move your right leg at all, and do you feel any numbness or tingling in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial assessment notes pain in both knees, not just the right groin, which is a crucial distinction given the rear-end collision mechanism. Did you experience any immediate locking or inability to straighten your right leg when the pain started, and can you actively lift your right leg off the floor right now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation. The clinical presentation of a severe right groin pain following a rear-end collision, combined with the leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated, is pathognomonic for this injury. I am requesting an emergency Pelvis_and_Hip_X-Ray to confirm the dislocation and rule out associated fractures.
